title: Why can’t you remember being a baby? With Nicholas Turk-Browne, PhD

sentences.en: Can you remember your first birthday party?
sentences.zh: 你还记得你的第一个生日派对吗？

sentences.en: Or your first words?
sentences.zh: 还是你的第一句话？

sentences.en: Or the house you lived in when you were two?
sentences.zh: 或者你两岁时住过的房子？

sentences.en: If you can't, and I bet you can't, why not?
sentences.zh: 如果你不记得了，我敢说你肯定记不得，那为什么呢？

sentences.en: The mystery of what scientists call childhood or infantile amnesia has long puzzled researchers.
sentences.zh: 科学家们称之为童年健忘症或婴儿健忘症的谜团，长期以来一直困扰着研究人员。

sentences.en: The infant brain is an amazing learning machine.
sentences.zh: 婴儿的大脑是一个惊人的学习机器。

sentences.en: It takes us from helpless newborns to walking, talking preschoolers in just a few years.
sentences.zh: 在短短几年内，它就让我们从无助的新生儿变成了会走、会说的学龄前儿童。

sentences.en: But for some reason, virtually no memories of those formative years stick with us into adulthood.
sentences.zh: 但出于某种原因，这些形成期的记忆几乎没有一条能伴随我们进入成年。

sentences.en: Today, we're going to talk to a scientist who studies infant learning and memory.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们将与一位研究婴儿学习和记忆的科学家对话。

sentences.en: He has looked into why we don't remember our own earliest experiences.
sentences.zh: 他一直在研究为什么我们不记得自己最早的经历。

sentences.en: Are babies' brains forming memories at all?
sentences.zh: 婴儿的大脑到底有没有在形成记忆？

sentences.en: And if so, why can't we access them later in life?
sentences.zh: 如果是这样，为什么我们在长大后无法获取它们？

sentences.en: How does the infant brain make sense of the world?
sentences.zh: 婴儿的大脑是如何理解这个世界的？

sentences.en: What insights can studying infant learning and memory give us into learning and memory more broadly?
sentences.zh: 研究婴儿的学习和记忆能让我们对更广泛的学习和记忆有哪些启示？

sentences.en: And how are scientists using new brain imaging tools and techniques to explore all of these questions?
sentences.zh: 科学家们又是如何利用新的脑成像工具和技术来探索所有这些问题的？

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, the flagship podcast of the American Psychological Association that examines the links between psychological science and everyday life.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《心理学说话》，这是美国心理学协会的旗舰播客，旨在探讨心理学科学与日常生活之间的联系。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是金·米尔斯。

sentences.en: My guest today is Dr. Nicholas Turk Brown, a professor of psychology and director of the Wu Tsai Institute at Yale University.
sentences.zh: 我今天的嘉宾是尼古拉斯·特克·布朗博士，他是耶鲁大学心理学教授兼吴蔡研究所所长。

sentences.en: He studies how adults, children, and babies perceive the world and how we learn from experience and store information in memory.
sentences.zh: 他研究成年人、儿童和婴儿如何感知世界，以及我们如何从经验中学习并将信息储存在记忆中。

sentences.en: His lab has pioneered techniques for brain imaging in infants and toddlers.
sentences.zh: 他的实验室率先开发了针对婴儿和幼儿的脑成像技术。

sentences.en: His work has been published in leading journals and featured in major news outlets, including the New York Times and the Atlantic.
sentences.zh: 他的工作发表在各大顶级期刊上，并被《纽约时报》和《大西洋月刊》等主要新闻媒体报道。

sentences.en: He has received Young Investigator Awards from APA, as well as from the Vision Sciences Society, the Cognitive Neuroscience Society, and the Society of Experimental Psychologists.
sentences.zh: 他曾获得美国心理学协会以及视觉科学协会、认知神经科学协会和实验心理学家协会颁发的青年研究员奖。

sentences.en: And he recently received the Trolland Research Award from the National Academy of Sciences.
sentences.zh: 他最近还获得了美国国家科学院颁发的特罗兰德研究奖。

sentences.en: Dr. Turk Brown, thank you for joining me today.
sentences.zh: 特克·布朗博士，非常感谢你今天能来。

sentences.en: Thank you for having me, Kim.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请我，金。

sentences.en: What is the earliest age that most people can remember?
sentences.zh: 大多数人能记住的最早年龄是多少岁？

sentences.en: Now, some people claim to be able to remember things from their babyhood or very early toddlerhood.
sentences.zh: 现在，有些人声称自己能记住婴儿时期或极早幼儿时期的事情。

sentences.en: Is that even possible?
sentences.zh: 这真的可能吗？

sentences.en: Well, to figure out what early memories people have, scientists sometimes will conduct surveys or poll adults about what they remember from early in life.
sentences.zh: 嗯，为了弄清楚人们有什么早期的记忆，科学家有时会进行调查，或者对成年人进行民意调查，询问他们对早年生活的记忆。

sentences.en: And typically, the earliest memories that people report are around four to five years old and up.
sentences.zh: 通常，人们报告的最早记忆大约在四到五岁及以上。

sentences.en: Importantly, that's regardless of how old you currently are.
sentences.zh: 重要的是，这与你目前多大年龄无关。

sentences.en: So if you're 20 years old, that's true.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你今年20岁，这是真的。

sentences.en: If you're 70 years old, that's true.
sentences.zh: 如果你今年70岁，这也是真的。

sentences.en: There's a period of the first few years of life that we are largely amnesic about.
sentences.zh: 在生命的最初几年里，我们存在一段很大程度上处于健忘状态的时期。

sentences.en: I never say never.
sentences.zh: 我从不说绝不。

sentences.en: People sometimes report early memories and they may be real.
sentences.zh: 人们有时会报告早期的记忆，而且它们可能是真实的。

sentences.en: But the science suggests that memories from before that period, before three or four
sentences.zh: 但科学表明，那个时期之前的记忆，也就是三四岁

sentences.en: years old, are unlikely to be sort of pure memories that you're recollecting from a specific moment in your life.
sentences.zh: 之前的记忆，不太可能是那种你从生活中的特定时刻回忆起来的纯粹记忆。

sentences.en: Yeah, you talked about asking basically people who are adults how far back they can remember.
sentences.zh: 是的，你刚才说基本上是问成年人他们能记住多久以前的事。

sentences.en: But what if you talk to a seven-year-old or a five-year-old?
sentences.zh: 但如果你去问一个七岁或五岁的孩子呢？

sentences.en: Can they remember being one or two?
sentences.zh: 他们能记住一岁或两岁时的情景吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, sometimes they can.
sentences.zh: 是的，有时他们能。

sentences.en: I can say that from personal experience.
sentences.zh: 我可以从个人经历中这样说。

sentences.en: I can also say we are currently helped curate an exhibit at the Peabody Museum in New Haven, where there's a station where people can write or draw their first memories.
sentences.zh: 我还可以说，我们目前正在协助策划纽黑文皮博迪博物馆的一个展览，那里有一个展区，人们可以写下或画出他们的第一段记忆。

sentences.en: And it's a wonderful exhibit and station just to see kids interacting with their parents, talking about their early life.
sentences.zh: 这是一个很棒的展览和展区，能看到孩子们与父母互动，谈论他们的早期生活。

sentences.en: And so I think it's possible and scientifically understudied for how long in childhood can we retain early experiences and memory.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这是可能的，而且在科学上，关于我们在童年时期能把早期的经历和记忆保留多久，这方面的研究还不够充分。

sentences.en: I don't know for sure that we know the answer to that question because often people don't have
sentences.zh: 我不能确定我们是否知道这个问题的答案，因为人们通常没有

sentences.en: ground truth about what was actually experienced early in life that they can go back to and verify whether a memory was accurate or not.
sentences.zh: 关于生命早期实际经历的确凿事实，他们可以回过头去核实记忆是否准确。

sentences.en: And so that's where the scientific research comes in to try to establish on firmer ground that a memory is authentic and accurate.
sentences.zh: 这就是科学研究介入的地方，它试图在更坚实的基础上确定一段记忆是真实且准确的。

sentences.en: Well, let's talk about the question I asked in the introduction just a few moments ago.
sentences.zh: 那么，让我们来谈谈我刚才在引言中提出的问题。

sentences.en: Do we make memories as babies that we just can't access when we get older?
sentences.zh: 我们作为婴儿时是否创造了记忆，只是在长大后无法获取它们？

sentences.en: Or do babies not form memories at all, at least not in the same way that adults do?
sentences.zh: 还是婴儿根本不形成记忆，至少不是以成年人的方式形成？

sentences.en: Yeah, this is a profound and fascinating question that I think we have all thought about in one way or another as parents and as people thinking back on our early lives.
sentences.zh: 是的，这是一个深刻而迷人的问题，我想作为父母，作为回顾自己早期生活的人，我们所有人都曾以这样或那样的方式思考过这个问题。

sentences.en: I mean, this has fascinated scientists for more than a century.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这让科学家们着迷了一个多世纪。

sentences.en: Freud popularized the idea of infantile amnesia and had his own ideas about it that are not accepted today.
sentences.zh: 弗洛伊德普及了婴儿健忘症的概念，并对它有自己的看法，这些看法在今天并不被接受。

sentences.en: But basically, there are two general kinds of explanations which you're alluding to.
sentences.zh: 但基本上，正如你所暗示的，有两种大致的解释。

sentences.en: One is that maybe the infant's mind and brain are immature and unable to store durable memories.
sentences.zh: 一种是婴儿的心智和大脑可能还不够成熟，无法储存持久的记忆。

sentences.en: And so our lack of memories later in life are because there's nothing available for us to pull up.
sentences.zh: 因此我们晚年缺乏记忆，是因为没有什么可供我们提取的。

sentences.en: The other possibility is that the infant brain is storing memories and that over time we lose access to those memories.
sentences.zh: 另一种可能性是婴儿的大脑正在储存记忆，随着时间的推移，我们失去了获取这些记忆的通道。

sentences.en: And in some abstract sense, they may still be there in the brain if we could access them somehow.
sentences.zh: 从某种抽象意义上说，如果我们能以某种方式获取它们，它们可能仍然存在于大脑中。

sentences.en: And so these are the two sort of classic
sentences.zh: 所以，这些是关于婴儿健忘症的两种经典

sentences.en: hypotheses about infantile amnesia.
sentences.zh: 假设。

sentences.en: The first having to do with a failure of encoding or storing a memory.
sentences.zh: 第一种与编码或储存记忆失败有关。

sentences.en: The second having to do with a failure of retrieval of being able to access the memory.
sentences.zh: 第二种与无法提取或获取记忆有关。

sentences.en: And this is a longstanding question, but really excitingly, there's been amazing scientific progress in the last few years that have shed light on this question.
sentences.zh: 这是一个长期存在的问题，但非常令人兴奋的是，在过去的几年里，科学取得了惊人的进展，揭示了这个问题。

sentences.en: The most compelling recent research actually has come from animal studies in rodents.
sentences.zh: 最近最令人信服的研究其实来自于对啮齿动物的动物研究。

sentences.en: So to walk you through that briefly, imagine that you have a baby mouse and you give them some kind of memory.
sentences.zh: 简单地向你介绍一下，假设你有一只幼鼠，你给它留下某种记忆。

sentences.en: So for example, you put them in a maze and they have to learn how to escape from the maze.
sentences.zh: 例如，你把它放进迷宫里，它必须学会如何逃出迷宫。

sentences.en: If you then let that mouse grow up, and in the case of a mouse, that's not 18 years, that's 20 weeks or so.
sentences.zh: 如果你随后让这只老鼠长大，对于老鼠来说，那不是18年，而是大约20周左右。

sentences.en: And you put the mouse back in that same maze, they won't remember how to escape.
sentences.zh: 当你把老鼠放回同一个迷宫时，它会记不得如何逃跑。

sentences.en: That is, they show something like infantile amnesia.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，它们表现出了类似婴儿健忘症的现象。

sentences.en: They don't remember something they learned early in their life.
sentences.zh: 它们不记得自己生命早期学到的东西。

sentences.en: So the recent research though, used very fancy modern molecular methods to figure out how the initial infant mouse's memory had been stored.
sentences.zh: 然而，最近的研究使用了非常奇妙的现代分子方法来弄清楚最初幼鼠的记忆是如何被储存的。

sentences.en: And then after the mouse had grown up to stimulate the neurons that were part of that memory.
sentences.zh: 然后在老鼠长大会后，刺激构成该记忆一部分的神经元。

sentences.en: And they do this using a technique called optogenetics, where you shine light on neurons and it causes them to become active.
sentences.zh: 他们使用了一种叫做光遗传学的技术来做到这一点，即用光照射神经元，使其变得活跃。

sentences.en: So if you knew what neurons had stored a baby memory, and then you could activate those neurons in adulthood, what they found in these studies is that even though the mouse
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你知道哪些神经元储存了婴儿期的记忆，然后你能在成年期激活这些神经元，这些研究发现，尽管老鼠

sentences.en: couldn't remember how to escape from the maze normally, if you activated the memory through this kind of stimulation, then the mouse remembered and could escape.
sentences.zh: 正常情况下记不得如何逃出迷宫，但如果你通过这种刺激激活了记忆，老鼠就会想起来并能够逃跑。

sentences.en: And so what this suggested was that actually the memory was there.
sentences.zh: 因此，这表明记忆其实是存在的。

sentences.en: It's just being back in the environment wasn't sufficient to access it.
sentences.zh: 只是回到环境中还不足以获取它。

sentences.en: It needed to be directly stimulated.
sentences.zh: 它需要被直接刺激。

sentences.en: Now we can't do that in humans.
sentences.zh: 现在我们无法在人类身上做到这一点。

sentences.en: And I can tell you about the work in my lab that's trying to get at a similar question, but that evidence is suggestive of more of a retrieval
sentences.zh: 我可以向你介绍我实验室里试图探讨类似问题的研究，但这些证据更倾向于支持婴儿健忘症的提取

sentences.en: explanation for infantile amnesia that we may have latent forgotten memories that are still there in some fashion in our brain.
sentences.zh: 解释，即我们可能拥有潜伏的被遗忘的记忆，它们仍然以某种方式存在于我们的大脑中。

sentences.en: And is the reason we can't do it in humans because we basically have to open up their heads and go into their brains and start stimulating?
sentences.zh: 我们在人类身上做不到这一点的原因，是因为我们基本上必须切开头皮进入他们的大脑并开始进行刺激吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, indeed.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实如此。

sentences.en: There's a couple of reasons that the tricks to sort of tag which neurons are part of a memory require, you know, genetic and other sort of
sentences.zh: 有几个原因，用来标记哪些神经元是记忆一部分的技巧需要，你知道的，基因和其他一些

sentences.en: molecular tools that are not safe or ethical in humans.
sentences.zh: 在人类身上并不安全或不符合伦理的分子工具。

sentences.en: And the other is to stimulate neurons in the brain, deep down in the brain and the brain region that's really essential for this kind of memory called the hippocampus.
sentences.zh: 另一个原因是刺激大脑中的神经元，即大脑深处对这种记忆至关重要的被称为海马体的脑区。

sentences.en: You'd have to open up somebody's head.
sentences.zh: 你必须切开某个人的头部。

sentences.en: That's done in certain clinical conditions, for example, in neurosurgery for epilepsy.
sentences.zh: 这在某些临床情况下是可以做到的，例如用于癫痫的神经外科手术。

sentences.en: But for basic science studies, that kind of research where you knew what neurons were active in a baby's brain and then you stimulate them in adults is not
sentences.zh: 但对于基础科学研究，那种你知道哪些神经元在婴儿大脑中活跃，然后成年后刺激它们的研究所谓研究，在人类身上

sentences.en: currently possible in humans.
sentences.zh: 目前是不可能的。

sentences.en: Some people think that you can hypnotize people and regress them back far enough to retrieve these memories.
sentences.zh: 有些人认为你可以对人进行催眠，让他们退行到足够远的时间来检索这些记忆。

sentences.en: Is that scientific in any way at all?
sentences.zh: 这在任何程度上是科学的吗？

sentences.en: Or is that just a lot of hocus pocus?
sentences.zh: 还是这只是一堆哄人的把戏？

sentences.en: My initial reaction is hocus pocus.
sentences.zh: 我的第一反应是哄人的把戏。

sentences.en: But what I will say is that it's absolutely true that one thing that helps us to recall forgotten memories is to put us back in the same sort of mindset or context that we
sentences.zh: 但我要说的是，绝对真实的是，有一件事有助于我们回忆起被遗忘的记忆，那就是把我们带回我们

sentences.en: were when we initially encoded the memory.
sentences.zh: 最初编码记忆时的那种心态或语境中。

sentences.en: This is the idea of context that when you store memory, it's not only stored in terms of the content of what you're experiencing, that, you know, maybe the
sentences.zh: 这就是语境的概念，当你储存记忆时，它不仅根据你所经历的内容来储存，比方说，可能是

sentences.en: people at a birthday party or what flavor of the cake was and so on, but also kind of where you were in
sentences.zh: 生日派对上的人或者蛋糕的口味等等，还根据你在空间中的位置，一天中的什么时间或一年中的什么时间，世界上正在发生什么等等来储存。

sentences.en: space, what time of day or what time of year it was, what's going on in the world and so on.
sentences.zh: 所以我们的记忆深深地嵌入在我们体验它们的语境中。

sentences.en: So our memories are deeply embedded and the context in which we experience them.
sentences.zh: 引导你自己或其他所有人回到相同的心态以提示提取，绝对是一个非常有效的策略。

sentences.en: And it absolutely is a very effective strategy to kind of guide yourself or other people back to the same mindset in order to prompt retrieval.
sentences.zh: 我不知道催眠在这方面特别好还是特别坏，但是，

sentences.en: I don't know that hypnosis is particularly good or bad at doing this, but, you
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这就像经典的例子，如果你在找钥匙，想想你今天都去过哪里。

sentences.en: know, this is the classic, you know, if you're trying to find your keys, think about where you've been today.
sentences.zh: 所以我们自己会这样做，专业的记忆运动员也会这样做，他们使用

sentences.en: And so we do this ourselves and professional memory athletes do this as well, using techniques
sentences.zh: 诸如记忆宫殿法之类的技术，在脑海中追踪步骤来重建事情是如何被储存的。

sentences.en: like the method of loci, where you sort of trace steps in your mind to reconstruct how things had been stored.
sentences.zh: 所以这其中有一些道理。

sentences.en: So there's some truth to that.
sentences.zh: 是否有可能在较大的儿童或成年人中提供语境线索，

sentences.en: Whether it's possible to provide contextual cues
sentences.zh: 帮助他们恢复到婴儿时期的状态，这是一个更具挑战性的问题。

sentences.en: in an older child or an adult that would help them sort of get back into the same state they were in as a baby is a much more challenging question.
sentences.zh: 那么婴儿可能正在形成的记忆会怎样呢？

sentences.en: So what happens to the memories that babies might be forming?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它们在哪里？

sentences.en: I mean, where are they?
sentences.zh: 如果它们存在于大脑的某个地方，

sentences.en: And if they exist somewhere in the brain,
sentences.zh: 它们是否能以某种方式被检索出来？

sentences.en: could they somehow be retrieved?
sentences.zh: 在我们关于这个主题的研究（使用了功能性磁共振成像）之前，关于婴儿记忆的大多数研究都是行为研究。

sentences.en: Prior to our research on this topic, which used functional magnetic resonance imaging, most research on infant memory was behavioral research.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，发展心理学研究中有非常巧妙范式来试图探究婴儿的记忆。

sentences.en: And so there's very clever paradigms for several decades now in developmental psychology research to try to get at memory in babies.
sentences.zh: 这非常具有挑战性。

sentences.en: This is very challenging.
sentences.zh: 我们不能问婴儿：你还记得什么？

sentences.en: We can't ask a baby, what do you remember?
sentences.zh: 大多数婴儿，你知道的，在一岁以下或不会说话，无法回答这个问题，甚至可能不理解这个问题是什么。

sentences.en: Most of the babies, you know, under a year or pre-verbal and unable to answer that question or even maybe understand what the question is.
sentences.zh: 所以你必须使用间接的行为方法。

sentences.en: And so you have to use indirect behavioral methods.

sentences.en: So Roe v.

sentences.zh: 在成年人中，通过脑成像访问它的唯一方法就是通过功能性磁共振成像。

sentences.en: And usually you need to collect an hour or two hours of data in order to find the signal and the noise.

sentences.en: But when we did, we were able to study the hippocampus.
sentences.zh: 但当我们做到这一点时，我们得以研究海马体。

sentences.zh: 我们发现，从大约一岁开始，婴儿的海马体就开始参与存储至少能持续几分钟的情景记忆。

sentences.en: Overall, we saw this across our whole age range from sort of three months to two years.
sentences.zh: 总的来说，我们在从三个月到两岁的整个年龄段都观察到了这一现象。

sentences.en: But the effects were strongest in babies starting around one year of age where greater activity, brain activity in the hippocampus, when they were
sentences.zh: 但在一岁左右的婴儿身上，这种效果最为强烈：当他们在

sentences.zh: 经历新鲜事物时，海马体中更强烈的脑部活动与之后更好的记忆表现相关。

sentences.en: Now we measure their memory in this case based on increased looking at things they were familiar with.
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，我们是通过他们对熟悉事物的注视增多来衡量他们的记忆的。

sentences.en: So that's one clue that actually the core memory functions of the brain involved in episodic memory, those basic mechanisms for storing
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个线索：实际上，大脑中参与情景记忆的核心记忆功能，也就是存储

sentences.en: these really rich memories that we can feel nostalgic about and reflect on, that that sort of core machinery may be coming along online around one year of age.

sentences.en: What we know, we published this work a couple of months ago, and it's really opened up a lot of questions because as we talked about at the
sentences.zh: 据我们所知，我们在几个月前发表了这项工作，这确实引发了许多问题，因为正如我们在

sentences.en: beginning, people don't tend to report many memories before age four or five, but the machinery seems to be starting to work around age one.
sentences.zh: 开头所讨论的，人们往往不会提及四五岁之前的许多记忆，但这种机制似乎在一岁左右就开始运作了。

sentences.en: And so what happens to those memories that are formed, you know, one, two, three years old that makes them inaccessible?

sentences.en: as a cognitive psychologist, which is a blessing and a curse because I was naive and foolish enough to want to try this.
sentences.zh: 是一名认知心理学家，这既是幸运也是诅咒，因为我当时足够天真和愚蠢，才想去尝试这个。

sentences.en: And I convinced some really adventurous graduate students to help me with this.
sentences.zh: 我游说了一些非常具有冒险精神的研究生来帮我做这件事。

sentences.en: So Cameron Ellis was one of my first graduate students who's now a professor at Stanford.
sentences.zh: 卡梅伦·埃利斯（Cameron Ellis）是我的第一批研究生之一，他现在是斯坦福大学的教授。

sentences.en: And the lead on this memory study that I was talking about is Tristan Yates.
sentences.zh: 我刚才提到的这项记忆研究的负责人是特里斯坦·叶茨（Tristan Yates）。

sentences.en: She's now a postdoc at Columbia
sentences.zh: 她现在是哥伦比亚

sentences.en: University.
sentences.zh: 大学的博士后。

sentences.en: And we have a large team of students and postdocs who've been working on these projects.
sentences.zh: 我们有一个由学生和博士后组成的大型团队一直在致力于这些项目。

sentences.en: So there's no short answer other than a lot of trial and error, almost over a decade of efforts now.
sentences.zh: 所以除了大量的试错——现在已经经历了将近十年的努力——没有别的简短回答。

sentences.en: I started with the thought that we needed to engineer some really clever solutions for this.
sentences.zh: 我一开始以为我们需要为之设计一些非常聪明的解决方案。

sentences.en: But as I should have known, it actually all comes down to the soft stuff.
sentences.zh: 但正如我本该知道的那样，这一切其实都归结于软件层面的东西（即人际与软性工作）。

sentences.en: Having parents feel really comfortable, getting them to participate in the research to help in the procedures,

sentences.en: setting up the scanner environment to be really comfortable for the baby, having them bring comfort
sentences.zh: 将扫描仪环境布置得让婴儿感到非常舒适，让他们带上舒适的

sentences.en: items like pacifiers and blankies and stuffies, giving them bottles and snacks during the scans.
sentences.zh: 物品，比如安抚奶嘴、小毯子和毛绒玩具，在扫描过程中给他们喂奶瓶和零食。

sentences.en: You know, I have found goldfish hiding in our MRI room.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我曾在我们的核磁共振室里发现过藏起来的金鱼饼干。

sentences.en: It's really variable.
sentences.zh: 这真的非常多变。

sentences.en: In some ways, it's not what you want in science because no two sessions are alike.
sentences.zh: 在某些方面，这并不是你对科学的期望，因为没有哪两次测试是完全一样的。

sentences.en: We've scanned, we've done probably closer, more than 400 of these sessions now.

sentences.en: And it's now feasible.
sentences.zh: 而现在这已经是可行的了。

sentences.en: It's not easy.
sentences.zh: 这并不容易。

sentences.en: But before us, there were a couple of groups who were doing this kind of work.

sentences.en: She's Lynn,
sentences.zh: 她是琳，

sentences.zh: 巴黎的德汉·兰伯茨（DeHan Lamberts）、麻省理工学院的丽贝卡·萨克斯（Rebecca Saxe）以及其他人。

sentences.en: I've been pioneering these methods.
sentences.zh: 我一直在开创这些方法。

sentences.en: And so this is a growing field.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个不断发展的领域。

sentences.en: I think it's extraordinarily exciting.
sentences.zh: 我认为这非常令人兴奋。

sentences.en: There are unlimited questions about the baby's mind where by looking under the hood, you might be able to reveal
sentences.zh: 关于婴儿的心智有无限多的问题，通过一探究竟，你或许能够揭示

sentences.en: something about how their mind works before they're able to express themselves or behave in more sophisticated ways.
sentences.zh: 一些关于他们心智如何运作的奥秘，甚至在他们能够表达自己或以更复杂的方式表现之前就能做到。

sentences.en: I'm glad you've assured our listeners that no babies were harmed during this research.
sentences.zh: 我很高兴你向我们的听众保证，这项研究没有对任何婴儿造成伤害。

sentences.en: Absolutely not.
sentences.zh: 绝对没有。

sentences.en: We started this research right around when I had my own babies.
sentences.zh: 我们开始这项研究的时间正值我自己的孩子出生前后。

sentences.en: And although they were never formally participants in our studies because that felt like a conflict of interest, they guided everything we did.
sentences.zh: 尽管他们从未正式参与我们的研究，因为那感觉像是有利益冲突，但他们指导了我们所做的一切。

sentences.en: And in fact, often babies are unhappy when they come out of the machine because they're looking at really interesting things and they're very comfortable.
sentences.zh: 事实上，婴儿在从机器里出来时往往很不高兴，因为他们在里面看着非常有趣的东西，而且非常舒服。

sentences.en: I'd say about a third of the time, the babies fall asleep and have a nap after 10 or 15 minutes in there.
sentences.zh: 我想大约有三分之一的时间，婴儿在里面待了10到15分钟后会睡着并小睡一会儿。

sentences.en: So they're quite comfortable.
sentences.zh: 所以他们非常舒服。

sentences.en: And actually, we've had parents ask us if we could just let them sleep a bit longer in the machine.
sentences.zh: 事实上，曾有家长问我们是否能让他们在机器里多睡一会儿。

sentences.en: Now, I mean, but isn't there that really loud noise through the whole experience?
sentences.zh: 现在，我的意思是，难道在整个体验过程中没有那种非常响亮的噪音吗？

sentences.en: Are they dealing with that?
sentences.zh: 他们能应付得了吗？

sentences.en: I mean, this sounds trivial, but it took a couple of years of work, how to apply hearing protection

sentences.en: in a way that would be durable and safe and redundant.
sentences.zh: 使其既持久、安全又具有冗余性。

sentences.en: And so we came up with a system that involves three layers of hearing protection.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们设计了一个包含三层听力保护的系统。

sentences.en: And we can attenuate the sound levels down to everyday sound levels that a baby might encounter on a sidewalk or in daycare and so on.
sentences.zh: 我们可以将音量衰减到婴儿在人行道上或日托中心等地方可能会遇到的日常音量水平。

sentences.en: And we know that it works because they don't startle when the machine turns on.
sentences.zh: 我们知道这很有效，因为当机器启动时他们并没有被吓到。

sentences.en: They're quite comfortable and babies are not shy about telling you when they're surprised about a noise.
sentences.zh: 他们非常舒适，而且婴儿在对噪音感到惊讶时是不会吝于表达的。

sentences.en: And so that part's working quite well.
sentences.zh: 所以这部分运行得相当好。

sentences.en: And really excitingly, we just developed with a company noise canceling headphones for babies.
sentences.zh: 而且非常令人兴奋的是，我们刚刚与一家公司合作开发了婴儿降噪耳机。

sentences.en: In the past, we've used a lot of hearing protection to make sure that the machine noise wasn't too loud.
sentences.zh: 过去，我们使用了大量的听力保护措施来确保机器噪音不会太大。

sentences.en: But now we have headphones that can play sound.
sentences.zh: 但现在我们有了可以播放声音的耳机。

sentences.en: So it's not just silent to them.
sentences.zh: 所以对他们来说不仅是安静的，

sentences.en: And we can look at really interesting questions around language and multi-sensory processing and so on.
sentences.zh: 我们还可以研究围绕语言和多感觉处理等非常有趣的问题。

sentences.en: So we're still evolving our techniques, but that's a great example of something that seems not especially technical or sophisticated, but that makes all
sentences.zh: 所以我们仍在不断改进我们的技术，但这是一个很好的例子，它看起来不是特别技术性或复杂，但却对他们的舒适度起到了

sentences.en: the difference for their comfort.
sentences.zh: 至关重要的作用。

sentences.en: We're going to take a short break.
sentences.zh: 我们要休息一小会儿。

sentences.zh: 当我们回来时，我们将与特克·布朗（Turk Brown）博士谈谈脑成像研究还能告诉我们关于婴儿如何体验世界以及

sentences.zh: 作为婴儿是什么感觉的更多信息。

sentences.en: What else might brain imaging research be able to tell us about how babies experience the world?
sentences.zh: 脑成像研究还能告诉我们关于婴儿如何体验世界什么？

sentences.en: I mean, could it give us insight into what it's like to be a baby and experience the world as a baby?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它能让我们深入了解作为婴儿是什么感觉以及如何以婴儿的视角体验世界吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, indeed.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实如此。

sentences.zh: 我的意思是，威廉·詹姆斯（William James）和其他人曾有过这样的观点，即婴儿的体验非常不同——那种繁盛、嗡嗡作响的混乱状态，以及其他观点。

sentences.en: And it's very hard, just like trying to study what a baby remembers.
sentences.zh: 这非常困难，就像试图研究婴儿记住什么一样。

sentences.en: When you can't ask a baby, I mean, you can't give them a complex task.
sentences.zh: 当你无法询问婴儿时，我的意思是，你无法给他们复杂的任务。

sentences.en: Indirect measures, whether they be behavioral, looking time, or reaching behavior, whether they be based on brain measurements, are the only option.
sentences.zh: 间接测量——无论是行为方面的、注视时间还是抓握行为，亦或是基于大脑测量的——是唯一的选择。

sentences.en: And so it's quite hard to know about the nature of an infant's experience.
sentences.zh: 因此，要了解婴儿体验的本质是相当困难的。

sentences.en: Like, what does it feel like to be a bat with very different sensory systems, for example?
sentences.zh: 比如，作为一个有着非常不同感觉系统的蝙蝠，会是什么感觉？

sentences.en: And there's an analogous question in infants.
sentences.zh: 婴儿身上也有一个类似的问题。

sentences.en: What's it like to be a baby?
sentences.zh: 当婴儿是什么感觉？

sentences.zh: 作为成年人，我们在哲学上很难看着一个婴儿并理解他们体验的本质。

sentences.en: But we can make some steps in that direction using advanced analysis approaches that have been developed in adult

sentences.en: cognitive neuroscience research to try to infer something about what a baby experiences.
sentences.zh: 试图推断出婴儿体验到了什么。

sentences.en: So to give you one example, one of Tristan's other studies was looking at a phenomenon called event segmentation.
sentences.zh: 举个例子，特里斯坦的另一项研究着眼于一种名为“事件分割”的现象。

sentences.en: And this is the idea that although we experience the world or the information we receive
sentences.zh: 这个观点是，尽管我们体验世界的方式或我们从世界接收到的信息

sentences.en: from the world is continuous, we're constantly flooded with sensory information, we experience the world actually in more discrete events.
sentences.zh: 是连续的，我们不断被感官信息淹没，但我们体验世界实际上是以更离散的事件进行的。

sentences.en: So for example, Jeff Zox at Wash U has a beautiful line of research over many years showing that if you present a movie to participants and you ask them to
sentences.zh: 例如，华盛顿大学的杰夫·扎克斯（Jeff Zacks）多年来有一系列非常棒的研究，表明如果你向参与者播放一部电影，并要求他们在

sentences.en: press a button when they feel like something has changed, like there's something has happened in the
sentences.zh: 觉得有什么改变时按下按钮——比如电影中发生了某事，有什么新事情正在发生——

sentences.en: movie, there's something new happening, people press the button at basically the same time.
sentences.zh: 人们基本上会在同一时间按下按钮。

sentences.en: That is, we perceive a continuous world in discrete ways, our mind sort of carves up our experience into events.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，我们以离散的方式感知一个连续的世界，我们的心智将我们的体验切分成各个事件。

sentences.en: And this is one way of asking about infant experience.
sentences.zh: 这是探究婴儿体验的一种方法。

sentences.en: Do they experience the world in events?
sentences.zh: 他们是以事件的形式体验世界的吗？

sentences.en: Or in the more James kind of ideas, it's all an undifferentiated mess, a jumble, a soup of experience.
sentences.zh: 还是按照詹姆士那种更接近的观点，这一切都是一团未分化的混乱、杂乱无章的体验之汤？

sentences.en: And so Tristan applied brain imaging methods that had been used to figure out when does the brain decide that a new event has started and apply that to infants watching a movie.
sentences.zh: 因此，特里斯坦应用了脑成像方法——这些方法曾被用来弄清楚大脑何时决定一个新事件已经开始——并将其应用到观看电影的婴儿身上。

sentences.en: And we had different ideas.
sentences.zh: 我们有不同的看法。

sentences.en: So maybe infants are just really, the way they experience the world is just totally dependent on the outside world.
sentences.zh: 也许婴儿只是……他们体验世界的方式完全取决于外部世界。

sentences.en: If there's a loud noise or a bright light or color or something changes in the world, they immediately sort of pivot and they're reactive rather than having an inner narrative of
sentences.zh: 如果世界有巨大的噪声、耀眼的灯光、颜色或某些变化，他们会立即做出反应，表现得具有反应性，而不是在内心对电影中发生的事情有一个

sentences.en: what's going on in the movie.
sentences.zh: 内在叙事。

sentences.en: And adults, we can use these methods.
sentences.zh: 而对于成年人，我们可以使用这些方法。

sentences.en: You can see that they, you know, might separate events every minute or two.
sentences.zh: 你可以看到他们可能每隔一两分钟就会分隔事件。

sentences.en: And so there's a question, do infants have kind of shorter, more reactive events?
sentences.zh: 所以这就产生了一个问题：婴儿是否拥有更短、更具反应性的事件？

sentences.en: In fact, we found the opposite, that infants tended to have more stable brain activity over time.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我们发现了相反的情况：婴儿随时间的脑活动往往更加稳定。

sentences.en: They carved up watching an animated movie into fewer events.
sentences.zh: 他们在观看动画电影时，将其划分成了更少的事件。

sentences.en: They seem to integrate more over time and have longer timescale experiences.
sentences.zh: 他们似乎在时间上整合得更多，并拥有更长时间尺度的体验。

sentences.en: So that's a question about the perception of time, about the continuity of experience.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个关于时间感知、关于体验连续性的问题。

sentences.en: It wasn't noisier, it was just longer.
sentences.zh: 它并不是更嘈杂，它只是持续时间更长。

sentences.en: And so that's the kind of thing we could do.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们能做的那类事情。

sentences.en: There are other techniques for brain decoding where you could try to figure out, well, here's what a baby's looking at, but what is being processed in different parts of the brain?
sentences.zh: 还有其他用于大脑解码的技术，你可以试着弄清楚：好吧，这是婴儿正在看的东西，但在大脑的不同部位正在处理什么？

sentences.en: And we can use machine learning or other AI-like techniques to infer the content of what they're experiencing.
sentences.zh: 我们可以使用机器学习或其他类似人工智能的技术来推断他们正在体验的内容。

sentences.en: So yeah, there's many possibilities in that direction.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，这个方向有许多可能性。

sentences.en: Ultimately, it's going to be hard to validate that that's the conscious experience of the baby without being the baby.
sentences.zh: 归根结底，如果不成为那个婴儿，将很难验证这就是婴儿的有意识体验。

sentences.en: But at least we can start to reveal some of what might be the contents of their experience.
sentences.zh: 但至少我们可以开始揭示他们体验内容的某些部分。

sentences.en: Where is that moment when you say, aha, that's a memory, the baby just remembered something?
sentences.zh: 那个时刻在哪里：当你大喊“啊哈，这是一个记忆，婴儿刚刚记住了某事”？

sentences.en: How do you know?
sentences.zh: 你是怎么知道的？

sentences.en: Because you're showing different images.
sentences.zh: 因为你在展示不同的图像。

sentences.en: The kid's in an MRI machine, right?
sentences.zh: 孩子在核磁共振机器里，对吧？

sentences.en: So you're not able to do eye tracking, right?
sentences.zh: 所以你无法进行眼动追踪，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, the child is in there.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，孩子在里面。

sentences.en: So how do you know, bingo, there's a memory?
sentences.zh: 那你怎么知道“太棒了，这里有一个记忆”？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So in this case, we are doing eye tracking in the machine.
sentences.zh: 所以在这个案例中，我们确实在机器里进行了眼动追踪。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So I didn't mention it, but there's an MRI safe camera that's positioned over their face.
sentences.zh: 所以我刚才没提到，但有一个兼容核磁共振的安全摄像头放置在他们脸部上方。

sentences.en: So they're lying in the machine.
sentences.zh: 所以他们躺在机器里。

sentences.en: If anyone's ever had an MRI before for your head or your brain, you're lying on your back.
sentences.zh: 如果有人以前为了检查头部或大脑做过核磁共振，你是仰面躺着的。

sentences.en: And so that's where the babies are too.
sentences.zh: 婴儿也是这样躺着的。

sentences.en: And they're looking up and there's a screen over their face.
sentences.zh: 他们向上看，脸上方有一个屏幕。

sentences.en: And so that's where we're presenting the images that they're looking at.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们呈现他们正在观看的图像的地方。

sentences.en: And there's a little camera sitting there that's tracking their eye movements.
sentences.zh: 那里有一个小摄像头在追踪他们的眼球运动。

sentences.en: So we adopt a technique that's widespread in developmental psychology and infant cognition research called visual paired comparison.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们采用了发展心理学和婴儿认知研究中广泛使用的一种技术，叫做视觉配对比较法。

sentences.en: So we'll present the baby with a series of individual images.
sentences.zh: 所以我们会向婴儿展示一系列独立的图像。

sentences.en: It could be a photograph of a face, a dog toy, a landscape, a series of these individual images to test their memory for those images after delay.
sentences.zh: 它可以是一张人脸的照片、一个狗狗玩具、一处风景，通过一系列这样的独立图像来测试他们在延迟后对这些图像的记忆。

sentences.en: And after other images, we have test trials in which we present two images at the same time.
sentences.zh: 在其他图像之后，我们有测试试验，在其中我们同时呈现两个图像。

sentences.en: So for example, the face that they had seen before alongside another face that they hadn't seen before on the other side of the screen.
sentences.zh: 例如，他们以前见过的人脸，旁边在屏幕另一侧放一张他们以前没见过的新人脸。

sentences.en: And in this kind of a task, after they'd only seen the face once before, we hypothesized that they would look more at the familiar face if they remembered it from before.
sentences.zh: 在这样的一项任务中，在他们只见过一次那张人脸之后，我们假设如果他们对它有记忆，他们会更多地注视熟悉的人脸。

sentences.en: If they didn't have a memory of seeing that face before, they should have no reason to look at one face more than the other.
sentences.zh: 如果他们对以前见过那张人脸没有记忆，他们就没有理由看一张脸多于另一张脸。

sentences.en: And so that's actually the behavior that we're measuring in that study, which is to measure
sentences.zh: 所以这实际上是我们在这项研究中正在测量的行为，即测量

sentences.en: how much they look at a repeated image on one of these test trials, and then go back and say,
sentences.zh: 他们在其中一个测试试验中对重复图像注视了多少，然后回过头来说：

sentences.en: what was happening on the brain for images where they showed this strong familiarity preference at the test?
sentences.zh: 对于那些在测试中表现出强烈熟悉偏好的图像，大脑发生了什么？

sentences.en: How did you get interested in studying this topic?
sentences.zh: 你是怎么对研究这个话题产生兴趣的？

sentences.en: As you mentioned, you're not a developmental psychologist by training.
sentences.zh: 正如你所提到的，你受到的训练并非发展心理学家。

sentences.en: So what got you on the path of studying memory in babies?
sentences.zh: 那么是什么让你走上了研究婴儿记忆的道路？

sentences.en: My lab started as a cognitive neuroscience lab focused on the adult or at least mature brain.
sentences.zh: 我的实验室最初是一个专注于成人或至少是成熟大脑的认知神经科学实验室。

sentences.en: And in particular, we're interested in trying to understand the coordination of different cognitive functions.
sentences.zh: 特别是，我们有兴趣了解不同认知功能的协调。

sentences.en: In cognitive psychology, we often study different aspects of the mind separately.
sentences.zh: 在认知心理学中，我们经常分别研究心智的不同方面。

sentences.en: You might study perception or attention or memory, but ultimately in the real world, all of these functions are intermixed.
sentences.zh: 你可能会研究知觉、注意或记忆，但归根结底在现实世界中，所有这些功能都是交织在一起的。

sentences.en: You know, we remember what we perceive and what we remember influences what we pay attention to or perceive.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们能记住我们所感知的事物，而我们的记忆又会影响我们所关注或感知的内容。

sentences.en: And so we started in my lab studying the interaction of different brain systems in support of cognition.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们在我的实验室里开始研究不同脑系统如何相互作用以支持认知。

sentences.en: And so I've long been interested in how humans learn and remember.
sentences.zh: 所以，我长期以来一直对人类如何学习和记忆很感兴趣。

sentences.en: And this isn't a profound insight, or at least it's not a unique insight, but we were studying this in adults.
sentences.zh: 这算不上什么深刻的见解，或者说至少不是什么独到的见解，但我们当时是在成年人身上研究这一点的。

sentences.en: And I think there's learning that happens throughout life.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为学习是贯穿一生的。

sentences.en: You know, I like to think that in my 40s.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我喜欢认为在自己四十多岁的时候也是如此。

sentences.en: But if you're really interested in learning, you can't ignore the first couple of years of life.
sentences.zh: 但如果你真的对学习感兴趣，你就不能忽视生命最初的几年。

sentences.en: This is this magical period of plasticity where we learn language effortlessly.
sentences.zh: 这是一个充满神奇可塑性的时期，我们在其中毫不费力地学习语言。

sentences.en: We learn how to walk.
sentences.zh: 我们学习如何走路。

sentences.en: We form social relationships, develop food preferences, focusing just on adults.
sentences.zh: 我们建立社会关系，培养对食物的偏好，而不仅仅把目光局限于成年人。

sentences.en: If you have an interest in learning and memory is leaving, you know, a lot of the variants off the table.
sentences.zh: 如果你对学习感兴趣，而记忆却在流失，你知道，这就排除了很多变数。

sentences.en: And so that's, that's kind of how I approach this to say, well, I'm, I'm also interested in developmental change and so on.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是我处理这个问题的方式，也就是说，嗯，我也对发展变化等等感兴趣。

sentences.en: But even as a, as a case study of saying, here is a brain of an infant that's learning and astronomically sophisticated, fast ways.
sentences.zh: 但即使作为一个案例研究，来说明这是一个婴儿的大脑，它正以惊人且复杂、迅速的方式学习。

sentences.en: And what do we understand about how that works?
sentences.zh: 对于这是如何运作的，我们了解多少？

sentences.en: We started from understanding how the adult brain learns and remembers.
sentences.zh: 我们从理解成年人的大脑是如何学习和记忆的开始。

sentences.en: I talked before about some of the brain regions that are involved in that.
sentences.zh: 我之前谈到过一些参与其中的脑区。

sentences.en: And when I got interested in working with infants and toddlers, there just wasn't a lot of research on those brain regions.
sentences.zh: 当我开始对与婴儿和幼儿合作感兴趣时，关于那些脑区的研究其实并不多。

sentences.en: Those are very well understood in adults, humans.
sentences.zh: 这些脑区在成年人类中已经被理解得很透彻了。

sentences.en: They're very well understood in animals, both young animals and older animals.
sentences.zh: 它们在动物身上，无论是幼年动物还是成年动物，也都已经被理解得非常透彻了。

sentences.en: But there just wasn't a lot of research on memory systems and early human development.
sentences.zh: 但关于早期人类发育中的记忆系统的研究确实不多。

sentences.en: And the reason is, is that most of them are deep in the brain, like this, like the hippocampus, the amygdala, the striatum.
sentences.zh: 原因在于，它们大多数都位于大脑深处，比如海马体、杏仁核、纹状体。

sentences.en: They're far away from the surface of, of the brain.
sentences.zh: 它们距离大脑表面很远。

sentences.en: And most of the existing methods for measuring, um, the infant brain used, uh, scalp-based measures like electroencephalography or EEG or functional neuroinfrared
sentences.zh: 而且现有的绝大多数用于测量婴儿大脑的方法，使用的是基于头皮的测量，比如脑电图（EEG）或功能性近红外

sentences.en: spectroscopy, F-NEERS.
sentences.zh: 光谱技术（fNIRS）。

sentences.en: And these are really powerful and good methods for measuring the cortical surface, but cannot resolve deep brain signals.
sentences.zh: 这些确实是测量皮层表面的强大且优秀的方法，但无法分辨深部脑电信号。

sentences.en: So the shorter answer to your question is, this is a fascinating period of life for learning and memory.
sentences.zh: 所以对你问题的更简短回答是，这是生命中研究学习和记忆的一个迷人时期。

sentences.en: And because of my training and background in adult cognitive neuroscience, I had expertise with the tools needed to measure the key brain systems, uh, in infants.
sentences.zh: 而且由于我在成人认知神经科学方面的培训和背景，我拥有测量婴儿关键脑系统所需工具的专业知识。

sentences.en: Do you think that your findings have implications for parents or preschool teachers or anyone else who is interacting with very young children?
sentences.zh: 你认为你的发现在父母、学前班老师或任何与极幼小儿童互动的人身上有什么启示吗？

sentences.en: I do.
sentences.zh: 我是这么认为的。

sentences.en: I mean, the, the research was done for basic science purposes, trying to understand, you know, the,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这项研究是出于基础科学的目的而做的，试图理解早期记忆的性质，以及一般的记忆，

sentences.en: the nature of, of early memory and, and memory in general, uh, memory is a fundamental part of who we are as the basis of our personality, our relationships or our expertise.
sentences.zh: 记忆是我们作为一个人的核心部分，是我们个性、人际关系或专业知识的基础。

sentences.en: Um, it's identity defining.
sentences.zh: 嗯，它是定义身份的。

sentences.en: And so I think in a basic science way, understanding how early experiences are, are learned and remembered is fundamental for understanding human nature.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，以基础科学的方式，理解早期的经历是如何被学习和记住的，对于理解人性至关重要。

sentences.en: Um, in a more applied way, I mean, I think parents are quite interested in understanding, um, uh, what they should do with their kids.
sentences.zh: 嗯，从更应用的角度来看，我的意思是，我认为父母非常渴望了解他们应该对孩子做些什么。

sentences.en: I think about this all the time, even things like when you should take that, that big vacation.
sentences.zh: 我一直在思考这个问题，甚至包括什么时候应该去度那个大假。

sentences.en: Um, are they likely to remember going out to, you know, going out West, um, if we go on a vacation before they're
sentences.zh: 嗯，如果我们去得太早，他们还不够大，他们还记得去西部旅行这件事吗？

sentences.en: old enough, um, do they remember, you know, meeting their great grandparent or their grandparent who's since passed away?
sentences.zh: 嗯，他们还记得见过后来已经去世的曾祖父母或祖父母吗？

sentences.en: I think parenting often we try to, we put a lot of pressure on ourselves to try to sculpt the experience of our kids in order to build the kind of people that we think we want
sentences.zh: 我认为在育儿过程中，我们常常试图给自己施加很大的压力，试图塑造孩子的经历，以便培养出我们认为我们希望

sentences.en: them to be.
sentences.zh: 他们成为的那种人。

sentences.en: And so I think this research suggests actually that even though we later in life don't
sentences.zh: 因此，我认为这项研究实际上表明，尽管我们长大后不

sentences.en: remember those first few years, actually there are memories being formed that are influencing our
sentences.zh: 记得最初的几年，但实际上有记忆正在形成，它们正在影响我们的

sentences.en: identity and our, our behavior, um, even if we can't sort of consciously recollect them.
sentences.zh: 身份和行为，嗯，即使我们无法有意识地回忆起它们。

sentences.en: So I think this emphasizes the, um, sophisticated cognitive abilities of infants and of toddlers.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这强调了婴儿和幼儿复杂的认知能力。

sentences.en: And it suggests that, um, we shouldn't think about memory as being a black hole for the first few years, but
sentences.zh: 并且这表明，我们不应该把记忆看作是头几年的黑洞，而是

sentences.en: rather it's there trying to understand where those memories go, how they get combined and how they influence our behavior.
sentences.zh: 应该去理解这些记忆去了哪里，它们是如何组合的，以及它们是如何影响我们的行为的。

sentences.en: Those are some of the questions that we're working on.
sentences.zh: 这些正是我们正在研究的一些问题。

sentences.en: Um, so yeah, that's the short answer, uh, a slightly longer answer.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，简短的回答就是这样，还有一个稍微长一点的回答。

sentences.en: You know, I won't, I won't go on too long, but just to say that many of the core things that we want kids to learn in more of a, you know, a daycare
sentences.zh: 你知道，我不会说太久，只是想说，我们希望孩子在日托中心

sentences.en: or a school setting are being learned via these memory systeMs. We talk about language acquisition or
sentences.zh: 或学校环境中学习的许多核心事物，都是通过这些记忆系统学习的。我们谈论语言习得，或者

sentences.en: learning about concepts or categories, learning about social relationships, that learning happens in these brain regions.
sentences.zh: 学习概念或类别，学习社会关系，这种学习就发生在这些脑区中。

sentences.en: And so if we want to understand both normative, how does the developing brain learn, uh, in, you know, in an ideal case in a healthy way?
sentences.zh: 因此，如果我们既想了解规范性的发育中的大脑是如何学习的（在理想情况下以健康的方式），

sentences.en: Um, also when things go awry in development, um, either early on or later, um, how does that impact knowledge and skills, language delays and so on?
sentences.zh: 嗯，也想了解发育过程中出现问题时（无论是早期还是晚期），这会如何影响知识和技能、语言迟缓等等？

sentences.en: If we had a better understanding of the underlying brain systems that absorb our experiences and build
sentences.zh: 如果我们能更好地理解吸收我们的经历并建立

sentences.en: memories, uh, that might point to some potential ways of either diagnosing or treating developmental disorders in the long run.
sentences.zh: 记忆的潜在脑系统，这可能会为从长远来看诊断或治疗发育障碍指出一些潜在的方法。

sentences.en: So what's next?
sentences.zh: 那么接下来呢？

sentences.en: I mean, are you continuing this same line of research?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你是在继续这条研究路线吗？

sentences.en: Are you expanding, moving into other areas?
sentences.zh: 你是在扩展并进军其他领域吗？

sentences.en: The study that I referenced before, which was, uh, published in Science in March, is a starting point.
sentences.zh: 我之前提到的那项三月份发表在《科学》杂志上的研究是一个起点。

sentences.en: This is showing that infants have the capacity to form episodic memories in the hippocampus beginning around one year of age.
sentences.zh: 这表明婴儿从一岁左右开始，就具备在大脑海马体中形成情景记忆的能力。

sentences.en: Because we were doing both the encoding and the retrieval in the same study, it was only a few minutes before they were tested on their memory.
sentences.zh: 因为我们在同一项研究中同时进行了编码和提取，所以在对他们的记忆进行测试之前，只有几分钟的时间。

sentences.en: So we know that they can store a memory, but we don't know how long it lasts.
sentences.zh: 所以我们知道他们可以储存记忆，但我们不知道它能持续多久。

sentences.en: And this is a really critical question when we think about, you know, our lack of early memories.
sentences.zh: 当我们想到我们缺乏早期记忆时，这是一个非常关键的问题。

sentences.en: We're really talking years.
sentences.zh: 我们谈论的其实是按年计算的时间。

sentences.en: It's our autobiography.
sentences.zh: 这是我们的自传。

sentences.en: And so it's an open question about how durable these early memories might be.
sentences.zh: 因此，这些早期记忆能持续多久还是一个未知数。

sentences.en: Maybe that's part of the explanation.
sentences.zh: 也许这就是部分解释。

sentences.en: It's also unclear if they are durable, why can't we access them?
sentences.zh: 目前尚不清楚的是，如果它们是持久的，为什么我们无法获取它们？

sentences.en: The mouse study I mentioned before suggests they're there.
sentences.zh: 我前面提到的小鼠研究表明它们是在那里的。

sentences.en: Uh, we're, I'm not suggesting we should go around stimulating the brains of humans to try to remember being a baby, but maybe we could figure out some clues from that mouse study.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们，我并不是建议我们应该到处刺激人类的大脑来试图记住当婴儿时的情景，但也许我们可以从那项小鼠研究中找到一些线索。

sentences.en: Just putting the mouse back in the maze wasn't enough to recall the memory.
sentences.zh: 仅仅把小鼠放回迷宫中是不够的，不足以唤起记忆。

sentences.en: That is the sensory cues.
sentences.zh: 也就是感觉线索。

sentences.en: You know, the landmarks in the environment, the geometry of the maze, maybe the smell of that room.
sentences.zh: 你知道，环境中的地标，迷宫的几何形状，也许还有那个房间的气味。

sentences.en: That wasn't enough to pull up the memory.
sentences.zh: 这还不足以提取出记忆。

sentences.en: And I think something very much like that happens in us that as a baby, we have an experience.
sentences.zh: 我认为在我们身上发生的事情与此非常相似，作为一个婴儿，我们有了一段经历。

sentences.en: Maybe you go to a grandparent's house and you're, I don't know, maybe a year old and maybe you're sitting up or lying down.

sentences.en: Um, you're missing certain categories to make sense of the objects in your environment, but your hippocampus is storing a memory.

sentences.en: That's what our findings suggeSt. So it's creating a snapshot of the sense that the rest of your brain is making of that experience.

sentences.en: The hippocampus gets input from the cortex and just takes a sort of a picture of what the rest of the brain is processing.
sentences.zh: 海马体从皮层接收输入，并拍下一张关于大脑其余部分正在处理什么内容的“照片”。

sentences.en: And now imagine you grow up and you're five years old or, you know, 20 years old, and you go back to your grandparents' house.
sentences.zh: 现在想象一下，你长大了，五岁了，或者，你知道，二十岁了，你回到了祖父母的家。

sentences.en: Um, it's the same, uh, sensory information, but it's not calling up that infant experience that we had.

sentences.en: And, uh, the hypothesis that we're pursuing is that it's because, um, how the rest of the brain develops influences the input that the hippocampus gets.

sentences.en: So now you can understand the conversation, you're taller and you're walking around.

sentences.en: So you're seeing different things.
sentences.zh: 所以你看到了不同的东西。

sentences.en: You have certain concepts and categories that you didn't have before.
sentences.zh: 你拥有了以前没有的一些概念和类别。

sentences.en: That becomes the input to the hippocampus.
sentences.zh: 这就成了海马体的输入。

sentences.en: That's like, um, what you're searching for in a, in a search engine.

sentences.en: Those are the terms that you're using to try to look up the memory, but that's not the content of your original memory.

sentences.en: Cause you couldn't make sense of what was happening.
